## Key claims (index)

- TNB RP4 Peak window is **2:00 PM – 10:00 PM**, 8 hours/day Mon–Fri; Off-Peak "expanded by 80% to 128 hrs/wk" (Section 1).
- MV Peak Maximum Demand charge under RP4 is **RM 89.27 – 97.06 /kW**, "+115% to +201% increase over legacy tariffs" (Sections 1, 3; chart: legacy 30.30 / 45.10 vs RP4 89.27 / 97.06 for MV Gen / MV TOU).
- NEM 3.0 closed 30 June 2025; from 1 January 2026 two mutually exclusive behind-the-meter pathways: **Solar ATAP** (GP/ST/No. 60/2025; export credited at Average SMP ~18.8–24.8 sen/kWh, capped at 1 MWac) and **Enhanced SELCO** (GP/ST/No. 51/2024 Pin. 1/2026; zero export, no capacity cap, RM 12/kWp/month Standby Charge and Mandatory BESS above 1 MWac) (Section 2).
- ATAP MAQ (kWh) = Capacity (kWac) × 5 Hours × Days in Month; default 800 kWac × 30 days = 120,000 kWh, worth RM 22,932 at RM 0.1911/kWh SMP (Section 2).
- Solar alone does not cut billed peak MD on an MV factory; a 400 kW BESS shaving the 2 PM – 10 PM peak saves RM 97.06/kW × 400 kW = RM 38,824/month (RM 465,888/year) in the simulator (hard-coded result; Section 3).
- **18 September 2026 CRESS Acceleration Package**: firm-supply System Access Charge cut from 25 sen/kWh to **14 sen/kWh**; plants must have ≥50% / 4-hour BESS, minimum 10-year PPAs, COD by **31 December 2028**; non-firm (solar without BESS) SAC 45 sen/kWh (Section 4).
- CRESS needs 5 mandatory agreements: BESC, CRESA, RE SAA, Back-feed Agreement, NEDA Agreement (Deed of Accession) (Section 4).
- CRESS calculator default: 38.0 sen/kWh PPA − 14 sen SAC = 24.0 sen/kWh net; 75 GWh/yr → RM 18.00 Mil/yr; 14.6% off-taker saving vs HV Tariff C4 Peak Rate 44.52 sen/kWh (Section 4).
- Fiscal "cliff" on **31 December 2026**: 100% GITA (Tier 1) for BESS, 60% GITA (Tier 2) for solar PV, 70% GITE income tax exemption for Solar Leasing; stacking GITA with Capital Allowance recovers **38.4% of Solar PV capex** and **48.0% of BESS capex** at 24% tax (Section 5).
- Tax calculator default: RM 2,000,000 solar + RM 1,000,000 BESS → RM 1,248,000 total cash tax savings, RM 1,752,000 net effective capex (Section 5).
- TNB CAS fee by tier: RM 0 (≤72 kWac), RM 1,000 (>72–180), RM 5,000 (>180–425), RM 8,000 (>425–1,000), RM 15,000 – RM 20,000 (>1,000–5,000 kWac); ST Section 9 license mandatory above 72 kWac; BESS mandatory above 1,000 kWac (Section 6).
- SARE (tripartite via TNBX) carries a fixed 2 sen/kWh TNB fee (~6–8% of gross revenue); Private Bilateral Hybrid PPA pays RM 0 to TNB and allows shared-savings on MD peak shaving (Section 7).
- Four client archetypes: Q4 Tax Cliff buyers; LV C&I (Tariff B & D, payback 3.5–4.5 years against 50.68 sen/kWh + AFA); MV factories (Tariff C1/C2/E1/E2, hybrid BESS PPA); HV / data centres (CRESS, ≥30 MW solar + ≥50%/4-hr BESS, ~38 sen/kWh vs 44.52 sen C4 peak) (Section 7).

## 1. Executive Pulse — "Executive Summary: The Post-NEM Regulatory & Economic Paradigm"

Malaysia's Commercial & Industrial (C&I) solar landscape in 2026 has transitioned away from volumetric Net Energy Metering (NEM 3.0) subsidies toward unbundled, grid-stabilized self-consumption (**Solar ATAP** and **Enhanced SELCO**) and open-access wheeling (**CRESS**). Under Tenaga Nasional Berhad's **Regulatory Period 4 (RP4)** tariff overhaul and the strict **31 December 2026 fiscal incentive cliff**, dual-licensed **RPVSP** (Service Provider) and **RPVI** (Investor) contractors must integrate **Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)** to capture Maximum Demand peak-shaving revenue and protect project bankability.

### KPI cards

| Card | Headline value | Sub-text |
|---|---|---|
| TNB RP4 Peak Window | 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM | 8 Hours/Day Mon–Fri (Off-Peak expanded by 80% to 128 hrs/wk) |
| MV Maximum Demand Surge | RM 89.27 – 97.06 /kW | +115% to +201% increase over legacy tariffs under RP4 |
| CRESS Firm SAC Wheeling Fee | 14 sen /kWh | Sept 18, 2026 Acceleration Package (Reduced from 25 sen) |
| Combined Tax Shield (BESS) | 48.0% of Capex | 100% GITA Tier 1 + 100% Capital Allowance (Closes 31 Dec 2026) |

### Malaysian C&I Regulatory & Statutory Governance Architecture

| Agency | Role tag | Description (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|
| PETRA | Policy Ministry | Ministry of Energy Transition & Water Transformation. Sets national capacity quotas (Solar ATAP, GREENS MADANI), CRESS acceleration packages, and long-term targets (70% RE by 2050). |
| Suruhanjaya Tenaga (ST) | Technical Regulator | Issues binding guidelines (Solar ATAP, SELCO, CRESS), grants Section 9 Generating Licenses (>72 kWac), regulates Class A Contractors and Competent Persons under Electricity Supply Act 1990. |
| SEDA Malaysia | Quota & Registry | Administers the eATAP portal, manages RPVSP and RPVI directories, certifies GCPV/OGPV Qualified Persons, and verifies first invoices for GITE Solar Leasing tax exemptions. |
| TNB / Single Buyer / GSO | Grid & Utility | Conducts Connection Assessment Studies (CAS), manages bi-directional metering, enforces RP4 tariff schedules, operates NEDA, and administers SARE contracts via TNBX. |
| MGTC (MyHIJAU) | Tax Verifier | Evaluates and approves GITA Asset (Own Consumption) applications for solar (60% Tier 2) and BESS (100% Tier 1). Manages MyHIJAU green product directory listings. |
| MIDA & LHDN | Investment & Tax | MIDA evaluates GITA Project and GITE Solar Leasing applications. LHDN enforces statutory income set-offs (70% limit per year) and Capital Allowance claims. |

## 2. ATAP vs SELCO — "Behind-the-Meter Regulatory Framework: Solar ATAP vs. Enhanced SELCO"

Following the closure of NEM 3.0 on 30 June 2025, Suruhanjaya Tenaga established two mutually exclusive behind-the-meter pathways effective 1 January 2026. **Solar ATAP** (GP/ST/No. 60/2025) allows export credits at Average SMP (~18.8–24.8 sen/kWh) but caps system capacity at 1 MWac. **Enhanced SELCO** (GP/ST/No. 51/2024 Pin. 1/2026) permits unlimited system capacity for zero-export sites, but enforces a **RM 12/kWp/month Standby Charge** and **Mandatory BESS** for installations exceeding 1 MWac.

### Regulatory Framework Feature Comparison (Effective 1 January 2026)

| Parameter | Solar ATAP (GP/ST/No. 60/2025) | Enhanced SELCO ≤ 1 MWac | Enhanced SELCO > 1 MWac |
|---|---|---|---|
| System Capacity Limit | 100% 12-mo Avg MD, **Hard Cap 1,000 kW (1 MWac)** | Sized to actual load (Up to **1 MWac**) | No Cap (85% MD limit abolished) |
| Allowed Mounting | Rooftop, Carpark, Covered Walkways | Rooftop, Ground, Floating (Water Bodies) | Rooftop, Ground, Floating (Water Bodies) |
| Grid Export & Settlement | Export allowed; credited at **Average SMP** (~19 sen/kWh) on Base Energy Charge ONLY | Strictly Prohibited (Reverse Power Relay) | Strictly Prohibited (Reverse Power Relay) |
| Credit Rollover | NONE (Forfeited monthly; use-it-or-lose-it) | N/A (Zero export) | N/A (Zero export) |
| TNB Standby Charge | EXEMPT (RM 0) | EXEMPT (RM 0) | RM 12 / kWp / month |
| Mandatory BESS Rule | Optional (For peak shaving / ROI) | Optional (For peak shaving / ROI) | MANDATORY BESS (From 1 Jan 2026) |
| Application Portal & Fee | SEDA `eATAP` (**RM 7.50 / kW** fee) + TNB CAS | SEDA registration + TNB CAS + ST Notification | SEDA registration + TNB CAS + ST License |

## 3. RP4 & BESS Simulator — "TNB RP4 Tariff Overhaul & C&I BESS Peak Shaving Economics"

Under TNB's Regulatory Period 4 (RP4) schedule implemented on 1 July 2025, consumption charges were itemised into Energy, Capacity, Network, Retail, and Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) components. While Medium Voltage (MV) volumetric energy rates dropped, **Peak Demand hours were shifted to 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM**, and Peak Maximum Demand charges surged to **RM 89.27–97.06/kW**. Because morning solar PV generation falls in TNB's Off-Peak window (10 PM – 2 PM), **BESS integration is essential** to store excess solar and shave peak demand during the 2 PM – 10 PM window.

## 4. CRESS Open Access — "Front-of-Meter Open Access: CRESS & The September 18, 2026 Acceleration Package"

The **Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS)** allows Renewable Energy Developers (REDs) to sell green power directly to High Voltage (HV) and Medium Voltage (MV) corporate off-takers across Peninsular Malaysia's grid via NEDA. The landmark **18 September 2026 CRESS Acceleration Package** slashed the System Access Charge (SAC) for firm supply from 25 sen/kWh down to **14 sen/kWh**, establishing strict rules: plants must incorporate **≥50% / 4-hour BESS**, sign **minimum 10-year PPAs**, and hit COD by **31 December 2028**.

### The 5 Mandatory CRESS Agreements

| # | Agreement | Description (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bilateral Energy Supply Contract (BESC) | Direct PPA between RED and Green Consumer (Min 10-year tenure under Acceleration Package). |
| 2 | Corporate RE Supply Agreement (CRESA) | Top-up and backup retail supply agreement between Green Consumer and TNB. |
| 3 | RE Supply Access Agreement (RE SAA) | Grid interconnection and transmission access contract between RED and TNB Grid Owner. |
| 4 | Back-feed Agreement | Governs auxiliary station power imported by the solar plant and BESS facility from TNB. |
| 5 | NEDA Agreement (Deed of Accession) | Governs day-ahead dispatch scheduling with Single Buyer and SAC settlement. |

## 5. Tax Shields & Cliff — "Corporate Tax Architecture: Navigating the 31 December 2026 Fiscal Cliff"

Malaysia's green tax incentive architecture—jointly administered by **MGTC**, **MIDA**, and **LHDN**—provides a massive capital subsidy for C&I Solar and BESS. However, the current framework faces a hard statutory deadline on **31 December 2026**. By stacking **Green Investment Tax Allowance (GITA)** with standard **Capital Allowance (CA)**, corporate buyers recover **38.4% of Solar PV Capex** and **48.0% of BESS Capex** through corporate income tax offsets.

### Tax category cards

| Tag | Heading | Text (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|
| MGTC GITA Asset (Tier 1) | 100% GITA for BESS | 100% tax allowance on qualifying battery storage Capex. Sets off up to 70% of statutory income per year. Must be commissioned and submitted to MGTC before **31 Dec 2026**. |
| MGTC GITA Asset (Tier 2) | 60% GITA for Solar PV | 60% tax allowance on qualifying solar rooftop Capex for own consumption. Combine with Capital Allowance for 38.4% tax shield. MGTC window closes **31 Dec 2026**. |
| MIDA GITE Solar Leasing | 70% Income Tax Exemption | Exempts 70% of statutory income for SEDA-registered RPVIs offering Solar PPAs (>3 MW capacity) for 5 to 10 years. Must apply to MIDA before **31 Dec 2026**. |

## 6. CAS & BOMBA Rules — "Technical Grid Interconnection, Licensing & BOMBA Safety Regulations"

Connecting C&I solar and BESS systems in Peninsular Malaysia requires compliance with **Electricity Regulations 1994**, **MS IEC 60364**, and Suruhanjaya Tenaga licensing thresholds. Furthermore, installing rooftop solar and lithium-ion BESS on designated industrial premises modifies the building's fire hazard profile, mandating formal **Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM / BOMBA)** consultations and thermal runaway safety integration.

### TNB Interconnection Study (CAS) & ST Generating License Matrix

| Capacity Tier (kWac) | Required Interconnection Study | Regulated CAS Fee | ST Section 9 License | TNB Metering Fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 kW – 72 kWac | Exempt (CCC for domestic >15kW) | RM 0 | Exempt (Sec 54 Notification) | RM 0 (OPC) / RM 1,530 (LPC) |
| >72 kW – 180 kWac | Connection Assessment Study (CAS) | RM 1,000 | Mandatory ST License | RM 1,530 (LV) / RM 2,330 (MV) |
| >180 kW – 425 kWac | Connection Assessment Study (CAS) | RM 5,000 | Mandatory ST License | RM 1,530 (LV) / RM 2,330 (MV) |
| >425 kW – 1,000 kWac | Connection Assessment Study (CAS) | RM 8,000 | Mandatory ST License | RM 2,330 (MV) |
| >1,000 kW – 5,000 kWac | Connection Assessment Study (CAS) | RM 15,000 – RM 20,000 | License + Mandatory BESS | RM 2,330 (MV) |

### JBPM (BOMBA) Fire Safety & BESS Compliance
- **Designated Premises Fire Certificate:** Factories, warehouses, and shopping complexes must consult BOMBA prior to solar/BESS install to update their annual Fire Certificate (Form I).
- **Rooftop Firefighting Access:** PV arrays must maintain clear perimeter setbacks and access walkways deducted from usable roof space.
- **BESS Thermal Runaway Mitigation:** Enclosures must integrate SIRIM/IEC-certified fire suppression systems and gas detection.
- **Direct Station Alarm Linkage:** Automatic fire alarm switchboards must link directly to the nearest BOMBA Fire Station.

### Electrical & Structural Mandates
- **PEPC Endorsement:** Mounting structure C&S drawings and electrical single-lines must be endorsed by a BEM-registered Professional Engineer (PEPC).
- **Anti-Islanding Protection:** Inverters certified to MS IEC 62109 must trip within 2 seconds upon loss of TNB grid supply.
- **Reverse Power Relay:** Mandatory on all SELCO systems to prevent accidental export to TNB distribution lines.
- **In-House Competent Personnel:** RPVSP must deploy certified GCPV Qualified Persons, Class A Chargemen, and CIDB G7 registered personnel.

## 7. EPCC Playbook — "Dual-Licensed EPCC + RPVI Strategic Commercial Playbook"

Holding both **SEDA RPVSP** (Service Provider) and **SEDA RPVI** (Investor) credentials allows an operator to capture both upfront EPCC engineering margins and long-term PPA cashflows. This section compares **SARE** vs **Private Bilateral PPAs** and provides a dynamic Client Archetype Decision Matrix to structure high-conversion customer proposals.

### SARE vs Private Bilateral PPA

| Item | SARE (Tripartite via TNBX) — tag "TNB Billing" | Private Bilateral Hybrid PPA / Lease — tag "Direct Contracting" |
|---|---|---|
| Parties | Prosumer, RPVI Investor, and TNB. | Direct contract between C&I Customer and RPVI. |
| Billing & Collection | Consolidated into monthly TNB bill; TNB collects and remits payment to RPVI. | Direct invoicing by RPVI; RPVI manages credit risk. |
| Service Fee | TNB charges a fixed **2 sen/kWh** fee (~6–8% of gross revenue). | **RM 0 fee to TNB** (Saves full 2 sen/kWh margin for RPVI). |
| Default Enforcement / Contractual Flexibility | Default Enforcement: High bankability; non-payment triggers TNB power disconnection. | Contractual Flexibility: High; allows **shared-savings split on Maximum Demand (RM/kW) peak shaving**. |
| Best Used For | Pure rooftop solar PV projects on Tariff B, D, C1, E1. | Hybrid Solar + BESS installations on Tariff C2, E2, E3. |

## Calculators and interactive logic

### Calculator 1 — Solar ATAP Monthly MAQ Calculator (`calculateMAQ`)
- Location: Section 2 (ATAP vs SELCO). Runs on page load and on every input change.
- Inputs:

| Element | Label | Type | Default | Min | Max | Step | JS fallback if blank/0/NaN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| maq-capacity | Installed Capacity (kWac) [Max 1000]: | number | 800 | 1 | 1000 | (none) | 0 |
| maq-days | Billing Period Days: | number | 30 | 28 | 31 | (none) | 30 |
| maq-smp | Assumed Avg SMP (RM/kWh): | number | 0.1911 | (none) | (none) | 0.005 | 0.1911 |

- Constant: 5 hours per day.
- Formula:
  ```
  maqKwh   = cap * 5 * days
  grossVal = maqKwh * smp
  res-maq-kwh   = maqKwh.toLocaleString() + " kWh"
  res-maq-value = "RM " + grossVal (0 decimals, thousands separators)
  ```
- Static output text: "ATAP Rule Constraint — Cannot exceed actual monthly grid energy import (kWh). Forfeited if unused."
- Outputs at default inputs (computed by running the code logic): Monthly MAQ Cap = 120,000 kWh; Max Gross Export Value = RM 22,932 (exact 22,932.00). Same as the HTML placeholders.
- Additional computed points: 1,000 kWac × 31 days → 155,000 kWh, RM 29,621 (29,620.5); 800 kWac × 28 days → 112,000 kWh, RM 21,403.

| 'hybrid' (3. Solar + BESS Peak Shaving) | max(50, baseLoad[i] − solarGen[i] − bessDischarge[i]) | 800 | 400 × 97.06 | BESS Shaved 400 kW during Peak | RM 97.06/kW × 400 kW Shaved | "Solar + 400 kW BESS Discharge during 2:00 PM - 10:00 PM window"; "Shaved 400 kW of Peak Demand"; "Tariff E2 MD Rate" |

  ```
  sim-annual-savings = "RM " + (monthlySavings * 12) (0 dp) + " / yr"
  sim-annual-sub     unchanged ("Direct bottom-line RP4 savings")
  ```

### Calculator 3 — CRESS Developer Net Generation Revenue Calculator (`calculateCRESS`)
- Location: Section 4. Runs on page load and on input/select change.
- Inputs:

| Element | Label | Type | Default | Step / options | JS fallback if blank/0/NaN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cress-ppa | Contracted PPA Price to Off-taker (sen/kWh): | number | 38.0 | step 0.5 | 38.0 |
| cress-sac | System Access Charge (SAC) Category: | select | 14 (first option) | see options below | 14.0 |
| cress-gen | Annual Green Energy Generation (GWh): | number | 75 | step 5 | 75 |

  SAC options (value: label):
  - 14: "Firm Supply (Solar + ≥50%/4-hr BESS) - 14 sen/kWh"
  - 25: "Legacy Firm Supply (Pre-Sept 2026) - 25 sen/kWh"
  - 45: "Non-Firm Supply (Solar without BESS) - 45 sen/kWh"
- Constant: hvTariffPeak = 44.52 (sen/kWh; helper text "Competes against HV Tariff C4 Peak Rate (44.52 sen/kWh)"). Fixed display: "Mandatory BESS Requirement: 50% GEP MW / 4-Hours Duration".
- Formula:
  ```
  netRate        = ppa - sac                                  // sen/kWh
  annualRevMil   = (gen * 1,000,000 * (netRate / 100)) / 1,000,000   // RM million
  savingsPercent = ((44.52 - ppa) / 44.52) * 100
  res-cress-net-rate = netRate.toFixed(1) + " sen /kWh"     (label "Net Developer Revenue")
  res-cress-annual   = "RM " + annualRevMil.toFixed(2) + " Mil"  (label "Annual Gross Cashflow")
  res-cress-savings  = savingsPercent.toFixed(1) + "% Offset"    (label "Off-taker Savings vs Tariff")
  ```
- Outputs at default inputs (computed by running the code logic): 24.0 sen /kWh; RM 18.00 Mil; 14.6% Offset (14.645…%). HTML placeholders were "24.0 sen /kWh", "RM 18.0 Mil", "14.6% Offset".
- Other SAC options at default PPA 38.0 and 75 GWh (computed): SAC 25 → 13.0 sen /kWh, RM 9.75 Mil, 14.6% Offset; SAC 45 → -7.0 sen /kWh, RM -5.25 Mil, 14.6% Offset.

### Calculator 4 — Client Tax Recovery & Net Capex Calculator (`calculateTax`)
- Location: Section 5. Runs on page load and on input change.
- Inputs:

| Element | Label | Type | Default | Step | JS fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tax-solar-capex | Solar PV Investment (RM): | number | 2000000 | 100000 | 0 |
| tax-bess-capex | BESS Investment (RM): | number | 1000000 | 100000 | 0 |

- Constants: solar GITA rate 0.60; BESS GITA rate 1.00; Capital Allowance rate 1.00 (both assets); tax rate 0.24.
- Formula:
  ```
  solarGita    = solarCapex * 0.60 * 0.24
  solarCa      = solarCapex * 1.00 * 0.24
  bessGita     = bessCapex  * 1.00 * 0.24
  bessCa       = bessCapex  * 1.00 * 0.24
  totalSavings = solarGita + solarCa + bessGita + bessCa
  netCapex     = (solarCapex + bessCapex) - totalSavings
  all outputs  = "RM " + value (0 dp, thousands separators)
  ```
- Outputs at default inputs (computed by running the code logic): Solar GITA RM 288,000; Solar CA RM 480,000; BESS GITA RM 240,000; BESS CA RM 240,000; Total Cash Tax Savings RM 1,248,000; Net Effective Capex RM 1,752,000. Same as the HTML placeholders.
- Implied recovery rates: solar 0.60×0.24 + 1.00×0.24 = 38.4% of capex; BESS 1.00×0.24 + 1.00×0.24 = 48.0% of capex.

## Extraction notes

- **31 Dec 2026 "tax cliff" framing.** The header badge, Section 1 summary/KPI, all three Section 5 cards (MGTC GITA Tier 1 BESS, MGTC GITA Tier 2 solar, MIDA GITE Solar Leasing) and the "Q4 Tax Cliff" archetype treat 31 Dec 2026 as a hard statutory deadline. The report contains no mention of Budget 2027 or any extension. The task brief says other reports in the set state Budget 2027 changed this; not verified by this extractor. Cross-check before relying on the deadline.
- **Tax shield stacking is simplistic.** The 38.4% (solar) and 48.0% (BESS) figures are GITA rate × 24% plus a 100% Capital Allowance × 24%, presented as immediate "Total Cash Tax Savings" and a "Net Effective Capex". The calculator ignores the 70%-of-statutory-income annual set-off cap that the report itself states (MIDA & LHDN card; Tier 1 card). It also ignores CA timing (no schedule is given; "100%" is applied up front), assumes enough taxable profit, and applies no discounting. The 24% tax rate is assumed, with no source. The footer cites "LHDN GITA Guidelines", while the body says MGTC/MIDA evaluate GITA.
- **Load-curve billed MD is hard-coded and does not match the plotted curves.** Within the 2 PM–10 PM window (14:00–21:00), the actual maxima are: baseline 1,200 kW (matches); solar-only 1,150 kW at 17:00 (shown: 1,200 kW); hybrid 750 kW at 17:00 (shown: 800 kW).
  - So, in the report's own data, solar alone cuts the in-window peak by 50 kW (about RM 4,853/month at RM 97.06). This contradicts "Solar alone fails to reduce Peak MD".
  - Hybrid against baseline is a 450 kW reduction (RM 43,677/month; RM 524,124/year at RM 97.06), not the hard-coded 400 kW (RM 38,824/month; RM 465,888/year). The actual 1,150 → 750 kW drop against the solar-only curve does equal 400 kW.
  - The comment "Peak occurs at 16:00 - 17:00" matches the computed solar-only peak at 17:00.
- **BESS charging is not modelled, and there is no "excess solar".** Solar never exceeds load in the profile (smallest net load is 250 kW at 12:00). The narrative "store excess solar" therefore has no surplus to draw on, and the 2,700 kWh/day of discharge (400 kW × 6 h + 300 kW × 1 h) has no modelled charging source. BESS discharge starts at 14:00, when net load is only 750 kW, and stops at 21:00, when load is 500 kW. The 50 kW floor (Math.max(50, …)) never binds.
- **Initial-state mismatches.**
  - On load, button 3 ("Solar + BESS Peak Shaving") is styled as selected, but the chart and outputs show the baseline. `updateLoadProfile` is not called at start-up.
  - The placeholders say "RM 0 / month" and "RM 0 / year", while the JS writes "/ mo" and "/ yr". "Direct bottom-line RP4 savings" is never updated.
  - The CRESS placeholder is "RM 18.0 Mil", while the code writes "RM 18.00 Mil" (toFixed(2)). All other placeholders match the computed defaults.
- **Legacy tariff names.** The report uses pre-RP4 tariff codes B, D, C1, C2, C3, C4, E1, E2 and E3 alongside RP4 terms. The chart maps them to "MV Gen", "MV TOU", "HV Gen" and "HV TOU". Examples: "Monthly MD Charge Rate (Tariff E2)" is labelled "TNB RP4 Peak MD Rate"; "HV Tariff C4 Peak Rate (44.52 sen/kWh)"; the LV "50.68 sen/kWh + AFA". None of these rates is sourced.
- **"+115% to +201%" does not reconcile with the chart data.** MV Gen goes from 30.30 to 89.27 (+194.6%) and MV TOU from 45.10 to 97.06 (+115.2%). The HV categories rise only +6.9% (29.20 → 31.21) and +2.8% (43.60 → 44.82). The "RM 89.27–97.06/kW surge" in the Section 3 intro applies only to MV, although the sentence does not say so.
- **"Off-Peak expanded by 80% to 128 hrs/wk".** 128 h/wk is consistent with the stated 8 h × 5 weekdays of peak (168 − 40). An 80% increase would imply a legacy off-peak of about 71 h/wk. The report does not state the legacy peak or off-peak hours, so the figure cannot be checked from the report.
- **SMP figures differ.** The Section 2 intro gives "~18.8–24.8 sen/kWh", the table gives "~19 sen/kWh", and the calculator default is 0.1911 RM/kWh. No source or period is given. The MAQ formula (kWac × 5 h × days) is stated without a source. The calculator's min/max attributes are not enforced by the JS, and 0 days or 0 SMP silently fall back to 30 days and 0.1911.
- **CRESS SAC figures.** The report gives 14 sen/kWh firm (18 Sept 2026 Acceleration Package), 25 sen/kWh legacy (pre-Sept 2026) firm and 45 sen/kWh non-firm (solar without BESS). The 44% cut cited in an HTML comment matches (25 → 14). No source is cited.
  - The "14 sen/kWh SAC Active" header tag and the SAC chart are static, regardless of the option selected.
  - Choosing Non-Firm at the default 38 sen PPA gives negative values (−7.0 sen/kWh, RM −5.25 Mil) with no warning.
  - "Annual Gross Cashflow" is actually revenue net of SAC.
  - The off-taker saving compares the PPA price only with the 44.52 sen C4 peak energy rate (no off-peak or blended rate, no CRESA top-up or other charges). It does not change with SAC, which implies the developer bears the SAC.
  - The hvdc archetype adds a "≥30 MW Solar" minimum and a "≥51% Local RED SPV" requirement that Section 4 does not mention.
- **Markdown syntax inside HTML.** `**bold**` markers (Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7) and backticks around `eATAP` (Section 2 table) display as literal asterisks and backticks in the browser. This extract renders them as markdown bold or code.
- **ST licensing inconsistency.** The Section 2 table lists "ST Notification" for Enhanced SELCO ≤ 1 MWac. The Section 6 matrix and the ST card require a "Mandatory ST License" (Section 9) above 72 kWac, which covers most of the ≤ 1 MWac range.
- **HTML comments describe features that do not exist.** The "Visualization & Content Choices" comment promises a "CAS Fee lookup" and a "Tariff Savings" calculator; CAS is a static table and there is no tariff-savings calculator beyond the simulator. It also promises a tariff chart comparing "Energy and MD charges across LV, MV, and HV". The actual chart shows MD charges only, for MV and HV only. The "client proposal blueprint generator" is a fixed four-option text switcher.
- **No sources at all.** The report has no citations or source links. The footer's "Fully compliant with Energy Commission (ST), SEDA, TNB RP4, PETRA CRESS, and LHDN GITA Guidelines (2026)" is an unsupported claim. All fees (CAS RM 1,000/5,000/8,000/15,000–20,000; metering RM 1,530/2,330; eATAP RM 7.50/kW; standby RM 12/kWp/month; SARE 2 sen/kWh) are unsourced.
- **Possible typo and undefined terms.** "GITA/A application" (taxcliff archetype) looks like a typo for GITA Asset. These terms are never defined: GEP ("50% GEP MW"), OPC/LPC, CCC, TNBX, NEDA, GSO, "7-day load" / "5-day load" (lvsme archetype), and SARE (never expanded).
- **Tax stack chart tooltip.** The footer sums only the items in the tooltip. Under Chart.js default interaction settings (no mode is set in this code), hovering one segment probably shows only that segment's value as the "Total Tax Recovery". Not verified in a browser.
- **Script loading.** Chart.js is loaded from an unversioned CDN URL (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js), so how the page renders depends on whichever Chart.js version is current.

# R2 — Malaysia TNB Maximum Demand & C&I Mitigation Intelligence Portal

> Faithful, complete markdown extract of `malaysia_tnb_maximum_demand_c_i_mitigation_portal.html`. Body content comes only from the report. Extractor observations are confined to "Extraction notes" at the end.

## Key claims (index)

- RP4 (Regulatory Period 4) took effect 1 July 2025 and governs Peninsular Malaysia tariffs through 31 December 2027; it abolished legacy activity-based tariff codes in favour of voltage-categorised Non-Domestic accounts (LV, MV, HV). (Section 1)
- Maximum Demand (MD) charges are unbundled into a Capacity Charge plus a Network Charge: MV General RM29.43 + RM59.84 = RM89.27/kW; MV ToU RM30.19 + RM66.87 = RM97.06/kW; HV General RM16.68 + RM14.53 = RM31.21/kW; HV ToU RM21.76 + RM23.06 = RM44.82/kW; LV is volumetric (8.83 + 14.82 sen/kWh, "Bundled in kWh"). (Section 1 table)
- Header stat: "RP4 MD Tariff Hike +100% to +202%"; legacy bundled MD charges were RM30.30–RM45.10/kW; Section 1 says MD charges rose "by up to 202%". (Header, Section 1)
- ToU peak window compressed from the legacy 14-hour block (08:00–22:00) to 8 hours, 14:00–22:00 weekdays only; off-peak = 128 hours/week (76.2%). Monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) replaced the 6-month ICPT cycle. (Section 1)
- TNB MD = twice the largest kWh imported in any 30-minute block of the month (1,440 blocks per 30-day month); one 2,000 kWh block sets 4,000 kW = RM388,240/month on MV ToU. (Section 2)
- Power factor surcharge applies below 0.85 (LV/MV) or 0.90 (HV): 1.5% per 0.01 drop down to 0.75, plus 3.0% per 0.01 below 0.75. (Section 2)
- Switching MV General to MV ToU costs RM7.79/kW/month more in demand; break-even inequality E_total × (0.0409 × α − 0.0149) + 89.27 × MD_24h − 97.06 × MD_peak > 0; with unchanged peak, α > 36.43% + (190.46 × MD / E_total) (example: 500k kWh/mo, 1,000 kW needs > 74.5% off-peak); or a peak-window reduction > 8.03% (MD_peak < 0.9197 × MD_24h) makes ToU profitable. (Section 4, tab 1)
- PLC staggering of three 50 kW compressors saves 150 kW = RM 14,559/month on MV ToU. (Section 4, tab 2)
- Standalone solar PV "fails to guarantee" MD reduction (cloud transients; 18:00–22:00 dark peak); solar + BESS caps grid demand (chart: 1,200 kW standalone-solar peak vs 750 kW cap with BESS); SMP export value RM0.1881/kWh. (Section 4, tab 4)
- Central chillers are up to 60% of peak demand in commercial complexes, hospitals and cleanroom factories; TNB offers an MV TES tariff schedule. (Section 4, tab 5)
- EECA 2024 (Act 861), enforced 1 Jan 2025: ≥ 21,600 GJ over 12 months (~500,000 kWh/month, ~RM200k/month bill) = Regulated Energy Consumer; 21,600–50,000 GJ/yr → REM Class 1; ≥ 50,000 GJ/yr → REM Class 2; fines up to RM100,000. (Section 5)
- Budget 2027 GITA: BESS and Solar+BESS keep Tier 1 (100% ITA against 70% Statutory Income) through 31 Dec 2030, "~24% CapEx cash tax reduction"; standalone EE assets (VSDs, BMS, Chillers) removed effective 1 Jan 2027, CapEx to be incurred and submitted to MGTC on/before 31 Dec 2026. (Section 5)
- ROI estimator at defaults (MV ToU, 1,800 kW, 25% reduction): RM 43,677/month, RM 524,124/year, 518 kW AC inverter; the page's static placeholder shows 2.4 years payback / 1,825 kWh / RM 1,642,500, but the code computes 4.0 years / 2,288 kWh / RM 2,745,098. (Section 3)
- 12-month, 4-phase roadmap; Phase 3 claims Tier 1 GITA can "compress payback to 2–3 years". (Section 6)

## 1. The Regulatory Period 4 (RP4) Paradigm Shift

Section label: "Section 1". Context paragraph (verbatim; the asterisks are literal in the HTML):

> Context & Overview: On 1 July 2025, \*Suruhanjaya Tenaga\* (Energy Commission) and Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) implemented Regulatory Period 4 (RP4), governing Peninsular Malaysia's electricity tariffs through 31 December 2027. RP4 abolished legacy activity-based tariff codes (Tariffs B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3) in favor of voltage-categorized Non-Domestic accounts (Low Voltage, Medium Voltage, High Voltage). This section explores how RP4 rebalanced utility cost recovery by slashing per-kWh energy rates while dramatically elevating Maximum Demand (kW) charges by up to 202%.

### Key Pillars of the RP4 Tariff Rebalancing

- **Unbundled Capacity & Network Charges:** Legacy bundled MD charges (RM30.30–RM45.10/kW) were replaced by two separate grid infrastructure components: a *Capacity Charge* (generation reserve reservation) and a *Network Charge* (transmission/distribution line capacity), pushing Medium Voltage peak demand rates to **RM89.27/kW** (General) and **RM97.06/kW** (Time-of-Use).
- **Compressed Weekday Peak Window (14:00 – 22:00):** RP4 compressed the ToU Peak Period from the legacy 14-hour block (08:00–22:00) down to an 8-hour window on weekdays only. Off-peak hours now encompass 128 hours per week (76.2% of all hours), including the entire 08:00–14:00 morning shift and all weekend hours.
- **Monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA):** Replaced the legacy 6-month ICPT cycle with a dynamic monthly fuel pass-through, transferring global coal/gas price fluctuations directly onto monthly C&I energy bills.

### Chart 1 (see Charts): "RP4 Unbundled Demand Charge Comparison (RM/kW/month)" — subtitle "Excludes 1.6% KWTBB Levy"

### RP4 Tariff Master Reference Table

| MV General Non-Domestic | Tariff C1, E1, F1 | >1 kV to ≤50 kV | 29.83 | RM29.43 / kW | RM59.84 / kW | RM89.27 / kW | 24 Hours / All Days |

## 2. Physics & Mathematical Formulation of TNB MD

Section label: "Section 2". Context paragraph (verbatim):

> Context & Mathematical Mechanics: TNB does not bill Maximum Demand on instantaneous microsecond current spikes or motor starting inrush currents. Instead, TNB defines Maximum Demand as *twice the largest active energy (kWh) imported during any consecutive 30-minute block* in the billing month. This section presents the exact mathematical formulas governing interval demand, power factor penalties, and peak window integration.

### Governing formulas (three cards)

**Card 1 — "1. 30-Min Interval Integration"**

- Formula (HTML subscripts shown as `_`): `D_i (kW) = 2 × E_i (kWh)`
- Text, raw as written in the HTML (LaTeX not rendered): "In any 30-minute block $i$ ($t = 0.5\text{ h}$), active energy $E_i = M_{\text{end}} - M_{\text{start}}$ is integrated. Multiplying by 2 converts 0.5-hour energy into average active power demand in kW."
- Plain-text version: In any 30-minute block i (t = 0.5 h), active energy E_i = M_end − M_start is integrated. Multiplying by 2 converts 0.5-hour energy into average active power demand in kW.
- Footer line: "1,440 blocks per 30-day billing month"

**Card 2 — "2. Monthly Billed MD Lock-In"**

- Formula: `MD_billed = max_{i ∈ W} (2 × E_i)`
- Text, raw: "TNB scans all assessment blocks $W$. A single 30-minute interval where consumption reaches $2,000\text{ kWh}$ sets a $4,000\text{ kW}$ demand charge ($\text{RM}388,240/\text{month}$ on MV ToU) for the entire billing cycle."
- Plain-text version: TNB scans all assessment blocks W. A single 30-minute interval where consumption reaches 2,000 kWh sets a 4,000 kW demand charge (RM388,240/month on MV ToU) for the entire billing cycle.
- Footer line: "W = 14:00–22:00 weekdays for ToU"

**Card 3 — "3. Power Factor Surcharge Formula"**

- Formula (HTML uses √ and superscript ²): `PF = kWh / √(kWh² + kVArh²)`; plain: PF = kWh / sqrt(kWh^2 + kVArh^2)
- Text, raw: "If monthly average PF drops below $0.85$ (LV/MV) or $0.90$ (HV), TNB levies a penalty: $1.5\%$ surcharge per $0.01$ drop down to $0.75$, plus $3.0\%$ per $0.01$ below $0.75$."
- Plain-text version: If monthly average PF drops below 0.85 (LV/MV) or 0.90 (HV), TNB levies a penalty: 1.5% surcharge per 0.01 drop down to 0.75, plus 3.0% per 0.01 below 0.75.
- Footer line: "Threshold: 0.85 (LV/MV), 0.90 (HV)"

### Interactive 30-Minute Interval Load & Demand Simulator

- Subtitle: "Adjust energy consumption in a 30-minute block to observe how instant active power dictates monthly MD billing."
- Input: "30-Min Energy Import (E_i):" [number] kWh — default 500 (full logic in Calculators section A).
- Output cards (static placeholder text in the HTML): "30-Min Energy (E_i)" = 500 kWh; "Recorded MD (2 × E_i)" = 1,000 kW; "MV General MD Cost" = RM 89,270.00; "MV ToU MD Cost (Peak)" = RM 97,060.00.

## 4. Comprehensive C&I MD Mitigation Solutions

Section label: "Section 4". Intro (verbatim):

> Engineering & Operational Hierarchy: Reducing TNB Maximum Demand charges requires a structured progression ranging from zero-CapEx tariff arbitrage and operational scheduling to software-driven automated load shed, solar-plus-storage integration, and thermal decoupling. Select a solution tab below to explore technical mechanics, mathematical break-evens, and optimal facility profiles.

Tabs (tab 1 is shown by default; tabs 2–5 are hidden until clicked): "1. Tariff Arbitrage Math", "2. Operational DSM", "3. Granular EMS & Load Shed", "4. Solar PV vs Solar + BESS", "5. Thermal Storage (TES)".

### Tab 1 — Tariff Arbitrage Math: "Zero-CapEx Tariff Switch: MV General vs MV ToU Decision Boundary"

Text, raw: "Switching from Medium Voltage General (RM89.27/kW) to Medium Voltage ToU (RM97.06/kW) introduces a demand penalty of RM7.79/kW/month. To justify the switch, the off-peak energy savings ($2.60\text{ sen/kWh}$ discount) or demand reduction outside 14:00–22:00 must outweigh this differential."

Plain: ... the off-peak energy savings (2.60 sen/kWh discount) or demand reduction outside 14:00–22:00 must outweigh this differential.

**Governing C&I Arbitrage Inequality** (HTML subscripts shown as `_`):

`E_total × (0.0409 × α - 0.0149) + 89.27 × MD_24h - 97.06 × MD_peak > 0`

**Scenario A: Unchanged Peak Location (α constraint)**

- Text, raw: "If peak demand cannot be shifted out of the 14:00–22:00 window ($\text{MD}_{\text{peak}} = \text{MD}_{24\text{h}}$), the facility must consume at least **α > 36.43% + (190.46 × MD / E_total)** of its energy during off-peak hours to break even."
- Plain condition: MD_peak = MD_24h; break-even α > 36.43% + (190.46 × MD / E_total).
- Example box: "Example: 500k kWh/mo with 1,000 kW peak requires > 74.5% off-peak energy share."

**Scenario B: Peak Demand Shifted Outside Peak Window**

- Text, raw: "If process rescheduling reduces peak demand during 14:00–22:00 by just **> 8.03%** relative to morning/night demand ($\text{MD}_{\text{peak}} < 0.9197 \times \text{MD}_{24\text{h}}$), ToU becomes immediately profitable even at neutral energy splits."
- Plain condition: MD_peak < 0.9197 × MD_24h (peak-window reduction > 8.03%).
- Box: "Immediate savings on all morning & weekend demand spikes (billed at RM0/kW)."

### Tab 2 — Operational DSM: "Operational Demand-Side Management & Process Sequencing"

- Intro: "Operational DSM eliminates simultaneous concurrency of high-draw machinery during the 14:00–22:00 weekday peak window without requiring capital-intensive energy storage assets."
- **1. Morning Shift Pull-Down (06:00 – 14:00):** "Because electricity demand recorded prior to 14:00 carries zero MD charge on RP4 ToU, batch furnaces, autoclaves, extruders, and thermal pull-downs should be scheduled between 06:00 and 13:30, transitioning to low-draw holding modes before 14:00."
- **2. Hard-Wired PLC Motor Staggering:** raw: "Configure Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) with mutual-exclusion interlocks. Preventing three $50\text{ kW}$ air compressors from starting together in the same 30-min block saves $150\text{ kW}$, yielding **RM 14,559/month** in MD savings on MV ToU." Plain: three 50 kW air compressors; saves 150 kW; RM 14,559/month on MV ToU.

### Tab 3 — Granular EMS & Load Shed: "3-Tier EMS Architecture & Real-Time Trajectory Prediction"

- Intro: "Manual operational discipline fails over time. Deploying real-time Energy Management Systems (EMS) synchronized with TNB's 30-minute integration windows prevents accidental peak lock-ins through predictive algorithms."
- **Real-Time Interval Peak Projection Formula** (verbatim): `D_projected (kW) = 2 × [ E(t_e) + P_inst × ((30 - t_e) / 60) ]`
- Explanation, raw: "Where $t_e$ is elapsed interval minutes, $E(t_e)$ is cumulative kWh, and $P_{\text{inst}}$ is live kW draw. If projected demand exceeds target MD, the EMS automatically sheds non-critical AHUs or unloads chillers for 15 minutes."
- Plain: t_e = elapsed interval minutes; E(t_e) = cumulative kWh; P_inst = live kW draw. If projected demand exceeds target MD, the EMS sheds non-critical AHUs or unloads chillers for 15 minutes.

### Tab 4 — Solar PV vs Solar + BESS: "Solar PV vs. Solar + BESS: Overcoming the Cloud Transient & Evening Peak Trap"

- Text (verbatim): "Standalone rooftop Solar PV fails to guarantee Maximum Demand reduction on MV/HV tariffs due to afternoon cloud transients (sudden solar drops) and the 18:00–22:00 dark peak. Pairing solar with BESS secures peak shaving and avoids cheap SMP export loss (RM0.1881/kWh)."
- Chart 3 (see Charts): "Cloud Transient & Evening Dark Peak Comparison: Standalone Solar vs. Solar + BESS".

### Tab 5 — Thermal Storage (TES): "Thermal Energy Storage (TES) & Dedicated TES Tariff Optimization"

- Text (verbatim): "For commercial complexes, hospitals, and cleanroom factories, central chillers represent up to 60% of peak electrical demand. TES systems freeze ice or chill water during off-peak overnight hours (22:00–14:00) and discharge cooling during the 14:00–22:00 weekday window, enabling chiller compressors to shut down during high-tariff periods."
- **TNB Dedicated MV TES Tariff Incentive:** "Qualifying facilities utilizing thermal storage can apply for TNB's Medium Voltage TES tariff schedule, permanently shielding chiller compressor kilowatts from weekday peak demand surcharges."

## Calculators and interactive logic

### A. Interactive 30-Minute Interval Load & Demand Simulator (`updateIntervalSim`)

- Location: Section 2.
- Input: `simEnergyInput` — "30-Min Energy Import (E_i)", type number, default 500, min 50, max 5000, step 50, unit kWh. Fires on every input change.
- Constants: 89.27 (MV General RM/kW), 97.06 (MV ToU RM/kW).
- Formula (faithful to JS):

```
energy      = parseFloat(input) or 0
demand      = energy * 2                      # kW
costGeneral = demand * 89.27                  # RM
costToU     = demand * 97.06                  # RM
show "30-Min Energy (E_i)"      = energy (thousands separators) + " kWh"
show "Recorded MD (2 × E_i)"    = demand (thousands separators) + " kW"
show "MV General MD Cost"       = "RM " + costGeneral (en-US, 2 decimals)
show "MV ToU MD Cost (Peak)"    = "RM " + costToU (en-US, 2 decimals)
# code comment: "Update interval 27 (13:30) and 28 (14:00) in chart"
chart series data[27] = demand ; redraw      # only index 27 is written
```

- Not called on page load (only on input), so the static placeholders show first.
- Outputs at default inputs (computed by running the code logic): 500 kWh; 1,000 kW; RM 89,270.00; RM 97,060.00 — identical to the HTML placeholders. Chart index 27 would be set to 1000 (same as its base value).
- At max input 5000 (computed): 10,000 kW; RM 892,700.00; RM 970,600.00.

### B. C&I Maximum Demand Reduction & BESS ROI Estimator (`calculateROI`)

- Location: Section 3. Runs on page load and on every input change.
- Inputs:

| Input (id) | Label | Type | Default | Min / Max / Step or options |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calcTariff | Select RP4 Tariff Category | select | MV_ToU (selected) | MV_General = "Medium Voltage General (RM89.27 / kW)"; MV_ToU = "Medium Voltage ToU (RM97.06 / kW)"; HV_ToU = "High Voltage ToU (RM44.82 / kW)" |
| calcKwh | Monthly Energy Consumption (kWh) | number | 600000 | min 50000, step 50000, no max |
| calcPeakKw | Current Unmitigated Peak Demand (kW) | range | 1800 | min 300, max 5000, step 50 |
| calcRedPct | Target Peak MD Reduction Goal (%) | range | 25 | min 5, max 50, step 1 |
| calcGita | GITA Asset Tax Allowance Status | select | Tier1_100 (first option) | Tier1_100 = "Tier 1: 100% Investment Tax Allowance (BESS & Solar+BESS)"; None = "No Tax Incentives Applied" |

- Constants: MD rates 97.06 (default / MV_ToU), 89.27 (MV_General), 44.82 (HV_ToU); inverter safety factor 1.15; discharge duration 3.5 h; DoD 0.85; efficiency 0.90; SoH 0.90; turn-key BESS cost RM1,200 per kWh ("~RM1,200 per kWh"); GITA tax shield 24% of gross CapEx.
- Formula (faithful to JS, including code comments):

```
tariff, kwh, peakKw, redPct, gitaOption = inputs   # kwh is read but never used
label calcPeakKwVal = peakKw (thousands separators) + " kW"
deltaKw = peakKw * (redPct / 100)
label calcRedPctVal = redPct + "% (" + round0(deltaKw) + " kW)"

mdRate = 97.06                         # "Default MV ToU"
if tariff == "MV_General": mdRate = 89.27
if tariff == "HV_ToU":     mdRate = 44.82

monthlySavings = deltaKw * mdRate
annualSavings  = monthlySavings * 12

bessKw  = deltaKw * 1.15               # "Inverter Power rating (kW AC) with 1.15 safety margin"
bessKwh = (deltaKw * 3.5) / (0.85 * 0.90 * 0.90)
          # "Storage Capacity (kWh): Delta kW * 3.5 hours peak discharge duration / (DoD 0.85 * Eff 0.90 * SoH 0.90)"
grossCapex = bessKwh * 1200            # "Turn-key BESS Cost (~RM1,200 per kWh)"

gitaTaxShield = 0
if gitaOption == "Tier1_100": gitaTaxShield = grossCapex * 0.24
          # "GITA Tier 1 = 100% ITA against 70% Statutory Income at 24% tax rate"; "24% effective tax reduction"
netCapex    = grossCapex - gitaTaxShield
paybackYears = annualSavings > 0 ? netCapex / annualSavings : 0

cash[0] = -netCapex                    # not rounded
for y in 1..10: cash[y] = round(-netCapex + annualSavings * y)
```

- Output formatting and branches:
  - resMonthlySavings = "RM " + round(monthlySavings) with thousands separators.
  - resAnnualSavings = "RM " + round(annualSavings) + " / year".
  - resPayback = paybackYears to 1 decimal + " Years" if paybackYears > 0, else "N/A".
  - resGitaShield = if Tier1_100: "Includes RM {round(gitaTaxShield)} GITA Tax Shield"; else "No Tax Shield Applied".
  - resBessKw = round(bessKw) + " kW AC"; resBessKwh = round(bessKwh) + " kWh"; resGrossCapex = "RM " + round(grossCapex).
  - Cash-flow chart series = cash[0..10].

## Extraction notes

- Unrendered LaTeX: the page loads only Tailwind and Chart.js (no MathJax/KaTeX), so all `$...$` math shows raw on screen: Section 2 cards 1–3 (e.g. `$E_i = M_{\text{end}} - M_{\text{start}}$`, `$\text{RM}388,240/\text{month}$`, `$1.5\%$`), the Section 3 BESS sizing footnote (`$k_s = 1.15$`, `$\eta_{\text{dis}}$`, `$\text{SoH}_{\text{EoL}}$`), Section 4 tab 1 (`$2.60\text{ sen/kWh}$`, Scenario A/B MD conditions), tab 2 (`$50\text{ kW}$`, `$150\text{ kW}$`) and tab 3 (`$t_e$`, `$E(t_e)$`, `$P_{\text{inst}}$`). Plain-text versions are given in the body.
- Literal markdown asterisks: "\*Suruhanjaya Tenaga\*" appears with visible asterisks in the Section 1 context paragraph and the footer.
- BESS ROI placeholder vs computed mismatch (calculator runs on load, so the computed values are what users see): placeholder 1,825 kWh / RM 1,642,500 / 2.4 Years / "Includes 24% GITA Corporate Tax Shield" vs computed 2,288 kWh / RM 2,745,098 / 4.0 Years / "Includes RM 658,824 GITA Tax Shield". Placeholder figures are internally consistent with RM900/kWh (1,825 × 900 = 1,642,500; 1,642,500 × 0.76 / 524,124 = 2.38 years), not with the code's RM1,200/kWh and 3.5-hour sizing. Placeholders for monthly/annual savings and 518 kW AC match the code.
- BESS sizing duration conflict: the code sizes energy for 3.5 hours of discharge ("Delta kW * 3.5 hours peak discharge duration"), but the visible footnote says sizing is "across the 8-hour weekday peak window". Using 8 h in the same formula would give 5,229 kWh at defaults (arithmetic only).
- Safety factor k_s = 1.15 is applied only to inverter kW, not to kWh capacity, though the footnote lists it among the battery sizing factors. The footnote calls 90% "round-trip efficiency" but labels it η_dis (discharge efficiency).
- The "Monthly Energy Consumption (kWh)" input (default 600000) is read into `kwh` but never used in any formula; changing it has no effect.
- GITA tax shield is a flat 24% of gross CapEx in year 0; the code comment and Section 5 mention "100% ITA against 70% Statutory Income", but no 70% cap, utilisation timing or tax-rate input is modelled. Cash flow has no O&M, degradation, tariff escalation or discounting. Year 0 cash value is unrounded while years 1–10 are rounded.
- Payback claims do not reconcile: Phase 3 says Tier 1 GITA can "compress payback to 2–3 years" and the placeholder shows 2.4 years, but the calculator at its own defaults computes 4.0 years (5.2 years without GITA).
- 30-minute simulator writes the user's demand only to chart index 27 (13:30), which is outside the 14:00–22:00 window the chart title highlights; the code comment says "Update interval 27 (13:30) and 28 (14:00)" but index 28 is never written. The peak-window background colour array (`bgColors`, indexes 28–43) is computed but never applied, so no peak-window highlight is drawn.
- The simulator's "MV ToU MD Cost (Peak)" bills the 13:30 block at RM97.06/kW, although the report itself says demand before 14:00 carries zero MD charge on ToU (Tab 2; Scenario B "billed at RM0/kW"). The simulator also does not apply its own max-over-month rule: "Recorded MD" is just 2 × the entered block, regardless of the other 47 blocks in the profile.
- In the base profile the daily maximum (1,000 kW) sits at 13:30, just outside the peak window; the maximum inside 14:00–21:30 is 950 kW (observation from the array).
- Simulator subtitle says "instant active power dictates monthly MD billing", contradicting the Section 2 statement that TNB does not bill on instantaneous spikes but on 30-minute average demand.
- Tariff arbitrage figures recorded exactly as shown: inequality `E_total × (0.0409 × α - 0.0149) + 89.27 × MD_24h - 97.06 × MD_peak > 0`; α > 36.43% + (190.46 × MD / E_total); example 74.5%; > 8.03%; 0.9197. They reconcile arithmetically with the report's own table: 31.32 − 27.23 = 4.09 sen; 31.32 − 29.83 = 1.49 sen; 0.0149 / 0.0409 = 0.3643; 7.79 / 0.0409 = 190.46; 0.3643 + 190.46 × 1,000 / 500,000 = 0.745; 89.27 / 97.06 = 0.9197; 1 − 0.9197 = 8.03%. "Neutral energy splits" in Scenario B implicitly means the energy term equals zero (α = 36.43%). The 2.60 sen/kWh "discount" = MV General 29.83 − MV ToU off-peak 27.23.
- Other arithmetic checks that reconcile: RM7.79 = 97.06 − 89.27; RM388,240 = 4,000 × 97.06; RM 14,559 = 150 × 97.06; 1,440 = 30 × 48; 128 / 168 = 76.2%; 21,600 GJ = 6.0M kWh/yr = 500,000 kWh/month; 50,000 GJ ≈ 13.9M kWh; component sums equal each Total MD Rate.
- "+100% to +202%" MD hike (header) and "up to 202%" (Section 1) cannot be reproduced from the report's own figures: against the stated legacy range RM30.30–RM45.10/kW, the RP4 MV rates give +97.9% (89.27 vs 45.10) to +220.3% (97.06 vs 30.30), with 89.27 vs 30.30 = +194.6%. The report does not say which legacy rate maps to which RP4 rate.
- Legacy-code inconsistency: the context paragraph lists abolished codes "Tariffs B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3", but the table's legacy column also uses F, F1, F2, C3 and C4.
- Tariff table oddities to verify against the ST schedule (no source given): HV energy rates (43.03; 44.52/40.43 sen/kWh) are higher than MV (29.83) and LV (27.03); every ToU row has the same peak/off-peak spread (4.09 sen) and the same peak premium over General (1.49 sen). For LV, it is not stated whether the 8.83 + 14.82 sen/kWh capacity/network charges are included in or added to the 27.03 sen energy rate. Chart 1 plots LV General as 0 RM/kW (volumetric) and omits LV ToU, though the design comment says the chart compares LV, MV and HV General vs ToU.
- PF surcharge: the base the 1.5% / 3.0% surcharge applies to is not stated. The design comment promises a "Power Factor Surcharge Calculator" in Section 2, but none exists in the page.
- Design-comment vs page mismatches: "Dynamic Stat Ticker" is a static stat box; the rate table and EECA threshold assessment are static, not interactive; Section 4 is planned to cover "6 C&I engineering solutions" but has 5 tabs; the planned peak-window highlight is not rendered. The nav label for Section 3 has no "3." number; the calculator's input panel is headed "1. Facility Operational Parameters" with no "2." heading.
- Claims with no source citation in the page (only the footer's generic source line): Budget 2027 GITA restructuring (BESS/Solar+BESS Tier 1 through 31 Dec 2030; standalone EE removed from 1 Jan 2027; MGTC submission by 31 Dec 2026); EECA thresholds, REM classes and RM100,000 fine; SMP export RM0.1881/kWh; 1.6% KWTBB levy; chillers "up to 60%" of peak demand; TNB MV TES tariff "permanently shielding" chiller kW; turn-key BESS cost ~RM1,200/kWh (code comment only); "AI-sized BESS" (Phase 3).
- Undefined acronyms in the report: REM, MGTC, EECR, KWTBB, SMP, ICPT, AHU, VSD, BMS, ITA (ITA is expanded only in the calculator option text).
- Terminology: "cloud transient voltage sag" (design comment) describes a solar output drop, not a voltage event; Tab 5 describes off-peak as "overnight hours (22:00–14:00)", which spans the 08:00–14:00 daytime as well.
- Chart 3 x-axis labels are unevenly spaced in time (08, 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 21, 22) but plotted as equal categories.
- Chart.js is loaded from an unversioned CDN URL (`npm/chart.js`), so rendering depends on whatever version is current.
- `toLocaleString()` is called without a locale for most outputs, so separators follow the viewer's browser locale; the computed values above use en-US formatting.

# R3 — Malaysia C&I BESS Solutions & RP4 Maximum Demand Optimization

> Faithful, complete markdown extract of `malaysia_c_i_bess_solutions_dashboard.html`. Body content comes only from the report. Extractor observations are confined to "Extraction notes" at the end.

## Key claims (index)

- RP4 (governing Peninsular Malaysia through 31 December 2027) unbundles tariffs into LV, MV and HV tiers; MD charges split into a Capacity Charge (generation reserve) and a Network Charge (grid stress); a single 30-minute peak draw sets the MD charge for the whole month. (Section 2)
- Combined MD charges: MV General RM89.27/kW (anytime), MV ToU RM97.06/kW (peak window), HV General RM31.21/kW (anytime), HV ToU RM44.82/kW (peak window); LV is volumetric 23.65 sen/kWh. (Section 2 table)
- Moving from MV General to MV ToU raises MD rates by +8.7% (RM89.27 to RM97.06/kW) and peak energy to 31.32 sen/kWh ("The MV ToU Tariff Trap"). (Section 2)
- Under MV ToU, capacity and network charges are levied only on demand recorded 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM on weekdays; off-peak (10:00 PM – 2:00 PM and weekends) demand is exempt. (Banner, Section 2)
- BESS turnkey CapEx benchmark RM1,150 – 1,600 / kWh with 3–5 year payback for C&I facilities; simulator uses RM1,350/kWh average. (Banner, Sections 3 and 5)
- Budget 2027 GITA: 100% tax allowance, Tier 1 for integrated Solar + BESS (whole system), versus standalone BESS Tier 1 100% and standalone solar Tier 2 60% (14.4% effective CapEx reduction at 24% corporate tax). (Banner, Section 7)
- Case study: 500,000 kWh/month MV factory, 900 kW baseline MD, monthly MD + energy charges go from RM80,343 + RM149,150 (MV General) to RM48,530 + RM122,018 after ToU shift + 1 MWp solar + 250 kW/500 kWh BESS. (Charts)
- Simulator shows placeholder results RM 229,693 baseline, RM 170,748 optimized (-25.7%), RM 707,340 annual savings, RM 675,000 BESS CapEx, RM 162,000 GITA saving, 3.1-year payback; the code computes different figures at its defaults (see Calculators). (Section 3)
- ST licensing mandatory for BESS ≥ 5 kW under Electricity Supply Act 1990; Guidelines GP/ST/No.62/2026 mandate IEC 62619, IEC 63056, UL 9540A. (Section 7)
- BOMBA MS 2747:2024 requires a 2-hour fire-rated enclosure or separating wall for stationary BESS; Fire Certificate needed to keep industrial insurance valid. (Section 7)
- TNB/GSO: CAS study required for SELCO > 72 kWp; BESS mandatory for all new SELCO systems > 1 MWac; CRESS grid access charges 14 sen/kWh (developers) / 4 sen/kWh (consumers). (Section 7)
- Provider directory of 12 players: 6 EPCC/developers (Solarvest, Plus Xnergy, Ditrolic, Sunview, Gentari, Northern Solar), 2 integrators (EVOLTS, VertexSol3), 4 OEMs (Sungrow, Huawei, HyperStrong, LVK Power). (Section 5, Embedded data)
- Sizing heuristics: peak shaving at 10% – 20% of facility MD, 1 – 2 hours; solar clipping capture 2 – 4 hours; ride-through at 100% of critical load for 15 – 30 minutes. (Section 6)

## 2. Tariff Overview — RP4 Tariff Architecture & Maximum Demand Catalyst

Intro text: Under Regulatory Period 4 (RP4, governing Peninsular Malaysia through 31 December 2027), Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) and the Energy Commission (ST) unbundled legacy tariffs into Low Voltage (LV), Medium Voltage (MV), and High Voltage (HV) tiers. Maximum Demand (MD) charges are split into an explicit **Capacity Charge** (generation reserve) and **Network Charge** (grid stress). A single 30-minute peak draw recorded by smart meters during the billing cycle sets the baseline charge for the entire month.

### RP4 schedule table

| RP4 Tariff Tier | Legacy Mapping | Energy Charge (sen/kWh) | Capacity Charge | Network Charge | Combined MD Charge | Monthly Retail Fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LV General | Tariffs B, D, F | 27.03 | 8.83 sen/kWh | 14.82 sen/kWh | Volumetric: 23.65 sen/kWh | RM20 |
| LV ToU | Tariffs B, D, F (Opt-in) | Peak: 28.52 / Off-Peak: 24.43 | 8.83 sen/kWh | 14.82 sen/kWh | Volumetric: 23.65 sen/kWh | RM20 |
| MV General (row highlighted) | Tariffs C1, E1, F1 | 29.83 | RM29.43 / kW | RM59.84 / kW | RM89.27 / kW (Anytime) | RM200 |
| MV ToU (row highlighted) | Tariffs C2, E2, F2 | Peak: 31.32 / Off-Peak: 27.23 | RM30.19 / kW | RM66.87 / kW | RM97.06 / kW (Peak Window) | RM200 |
| HV General | Tariff C3 | 43.03 | RM16.68 / kW | RM14.53 / kW | RM31.21 / kW (Anytime) | RM250 |
| HV ToU | Tariffs C4, E3 | Peak: 44.52 / Off-Peak: 40.43 | RM21.76 / kW | RM23.06 / kW | RM44.82 / kW (Peak Window) | RM250 |

### Strategic ToU explanation (two callout cards)

- **The MV ToU Tariff Trap (Unmanaged Migration):** Migrating from MV General to MV ToU raises maximum demand rates by **+8.7%** (from RM89.27 to RM97.06/kW) and increases peak volumetric energy rates to 31.32 sen/kWh. Without active demand control or energy storage, an uncoordinated peak spike during weekday afternoons results in severe financial penalties.
- **The BESS + ToU Optimization Opportunity:** Under MV ToU, TNB calculates Capacity and Network charges **exclusively on peak demand recorded between 2:00 PM and 10:00 PM on weekdays**. Maximum demand spikes occurring off-peak (10:00 PM – 2:00 PM and weekends) are completely exempt. BESS discharges dynamically during peak hours to cap grid draw.

## 4. Dispatch Visualizer — 24-Hour Load & BESS Dispatch Simulation

Intro text: Simulate dynamic demand peak shaving between TNB's 2:00 PM and 10:00 PM Peak Tariff window.

- Dispatch Controls: buttons "Standard Peak Shave" (styled as active on load) and "Late Afternoon Spike".
- **Solar & Tariff Mismatch Notice:** Peak solar irradiance occurs from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM (Off-Peak tariff). TNB's expensive Peak Tariff starts at 2:00 PM and extends to 10:00 PM. BESS bridges this gap by charging midday and discharging from 2:00 PM to 10:00 PM to keep net grid draw below the dynamic MD target.
- Line chart of 24-hour profile (Chart 3).
- Three explanation cards:
  1. **Midday Charging (10am–1pm):** BESS absorbs excess solar PV generation or off-peak grid energy to prevent zero-export clipping under SELCO guidelines.
  2. **Peak Discharge (2pm–10pm):** AI-driven EMS releases stored energy when factory equipment startups risk breaching the pre-defined target threshold.
  3. **Capped Grid Demand:** TNB smart meter records the reduced net grid peak, locking in low Capacity and Network charges for the billing cycle.

### Operational Objective Sizing Matrix

| Operational Objective | Typical Power Rating (kW) | Discharge Duration (kWh) | Primary Driver & Application |
|---|---|---|---|
| Demand-Charge Peak Shaving | 10% – 20% of Facility MD | 1 – 2 Hours (0.5C – 1C) | Shaving 30-min rolling demand spikes from compressors, chillers, and stamping presses to eliminate RM89–97/kW fees. |
| Solar Arbitrage & Clipping Capture | Sized to PV Clipping Volume | 2 – 4 Hours (0.25C – 0.5C) | Capturing 10am–3pm SELCO/ATAP surplus solar to displace 31.32 sen/kWh evening peak energy draw. |
| Short-Interruption Ride-Through | 100% of Critical Process Load | 15 – 30 Minutes (2C) | Bridging voltage sags and brief grid trips for CNC machines, ovens, and automated assembly lines to prevent batch loss. |

## 7. Regulatory & GITA — Regulatory, BOMBA Safety & GITA Tax Framework

Intro text: Navigating mandatory Malaysian grid licensing, BOMBA MS 2747:2024 fire safety certification, and Budget 2027 tax allowance rules.

### Compliance cards

**Suruhanjaya Tenaga (ST) — Licensing & Safety Mandate**
- **Threshold:** Mandatory licensing for BESS ≥ 5 kW under Electricity Supply Act 1990.
- **Guidelines GP/ST/No.62/2026:** Mandatory IEC 62619, IEC 63056, UL 9540A certification.
- **Certification:** Form G (Completion) & Form H (Testing) signed by ST Competent Person.

**BOMBA Fire Safety — MS 2747:2024 Standards**
- **Fire Rating:** 2-hour fire-rated enclosure or separating wall required for stationary BESS.
- **Safety Clearance:** Mandatory thermal runaway suppression and isolation clearances.
- **Insurance Impact:** Fire Certificate (FC) is required to maintain valid industrial insurance.

**Grid Interconnection — TNB & GSO Regulations**
- **CAS Study:** Connection Assessment Study required for SELCO installations > 72 kWp.
- **Mandatory BESS:** Required for all new SELCO systems exceeding 1 MWac capacity.
- **CRESS Package:** Grid access charges set at 14 sen/kWh (developers) / 4 sen/kWh (consumers).

### Green Investment Tax Allowance (GITA) Comparison

| Parameter | Current Framework (2024 – 2026) | Revised Budget 2027 (2027 – 2030) | Strategic Financial Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standalone BESS | Tier 1: 100% GITA | Tier 1: 100% GITA | Yields direct 24% tax shield on battery CapEx against 70% statutory income. |
| Standalone Solar PV | Tier 2: 60% GITA | Tier 2: 60% GITA | Lower tax shield (14.4% effective CapEx reduction at 24% corporate tax). |
| Integrated Solar + BESS (row highlighted) | Assessed separately (100% BESS / 60% Solar) | Elevated to Tier 1: 100% GITA on entire integrated system | Major Catalyst: Pairing solar with BESS elevates solar CapEx allowance to 100%. |

## Calculators and interactive logic

### Calculator 1 — Interactive RP4 Bill & BESS ROI Calculator (`calculateSim()`)

- Location: Section 3 (ROI & Bill Simulator). Runs on page load (after charts are built) and on every input change.

Inputs:

| Input (id) | Label | Type | Default | Min | Max | Step | Options / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sim-tariff | Tariff Classification | select | MV_TOU | – | – | – | MV_TOU = "Medium Voltage ToU (Tariff C2/E2/F2) - RM97.06/kW"; MV_GEN = "Medium Voltage General (Tariff C1/E1/F1) - RM89.27/kW"; HV_TOU = "High Voltage ToU (Tariff C4/E3) - RM44.82/kW"; HV_GEN = "High Voltage General (Tariff C3) - RM31.21/kW" |
| sim-kwh | Monthly Energy Consumption (kWh) | range | 500000 | 50000 | 2000000 | 25000 | label shows value with thousands separators |
| sim-md | Baseline Peak Maximum Demand (kW) | range | 900 | 100 | 5000 | 50 | |
| sim-solar | Solar PV Capacity (kWp) | range | 1000 | 0 | 3000 | 50 | |
| sim-bess | Target BESS Shaving Capacity (kW / kWh) | range | 250 | 0 | 1000 | 25 | label shows "{bessKw} kW / {bessKw × 2} kWh" |
| sim-gita | Apply Budget 2027 GITA 100% Tax Shield (24% Corporate Tax) | checkbox | checked | – | – | – | |

Constants (rates by tariff; code comments in quotes):

| Tariff value | energyRate (RM/kWh) | mdRate (RM/kW) |
|---|---|---|
| MV_GEN (code default branch) | 0.2983 ("RM/kWh avg") | 89.27 |
| MV_TOU | 0.2886 ("blended peak/off-peak") | 97.06 |
| HV_TOU | 0.4200 | 44.82 |
| HV_GEN | 0.4303 | 31.21 |

Other constants: monthly fixed fee 200 (RM, added to both bills for every tariff); solar yield 115 kWh per kWp per month ("~115 kWh per kWp per month"); solar capped at 0.4 × monthly kWh; MD after BESS floored at 0.5 × baseline MD; BESS duration 2 hours (kWh = kW × 2); BESS CapEx 1350 RM/kWh ("RM 1,350 per kWh"); GITA tax rate 0.24.

Formula (faithful to the JS):

```
baselineMDCharge     = md * mdRate
baselineEnergyCharge = kwh * energyRate
baselineBill         = baselineMDCharge + baselineEnergyCharge + 200

solarGenKwh   = min(kwh * 0.4, solarKw * 115)
postSolarKwh  = kwh - solarGenKwh

postBessMD            = max(md * 0.5, md - bessKw)
optimizedMDCharge     = postBessMD * mdRate
optimizedEnergyCharge = postSolarKwh * energyRate
optimizedBill         = optimizedMDCharge + optimizedEnergyCharge + 200

monthlySavings = baselineBill - optimizedBill
annualSavings  = monthlySavings * 12
reductionPct   = round1((monthlySavings / baselineBill) * 100)

bessKwh      = bessKw * 2
bessCapEx    = bessKwh * 1350
gitaTaxShield = applyGita ? bessCapEx * 0.24 : 0
netCapEx     = bessCapEx - gitaTaxShield

paybackYears = annualSavings > 0
               ? round1(netCapEx / (bessKw > 0 ? bessKw * mdRate * 12 : 1))
               : 'N/A'

waterfall = [ round(baselineBill),
              round(baselineBill - (baselineMDCharge - postBessMD * mdRate)),
              round(optimizedBill) ]
```

Outputs displayed: "RM {round(baselineBill)}" (Baseline Core Monthly Bill); "RM {round(optimizedBill)}" (Optimized Monthly Core Bill); "-{reductionPct}% Total Reduction"; "RM {round(annualSavings)}" (Annualized Savings); "RM {round(bessCapEx)}" (Estimated BESS Installed CapEx); "RM {round(gitaTaxShield)}" (Direct Tax Savings via GITA Tier 1); "{paybackYears} Years" (Estimated Net Simple Payback Horizon); Chart 2 data.

## Extraction notes

- **Simulator placeholders differ from computed values.** HTML placeholders (RM 229,693 / RM 170,748 / -25.7% / RM 707,340 / 3.1 Years; Chart 2 bars 229693 / 205428 / 170748) are replaced on page load by calculateSim(), which at defaults (MV_TOU selected) gives RM 231,854 / RM 174,400 / -24.8% / RM 689,448 / 1.8 Years; bars 231854 / 207589 / 174400. CapEx RM 675,000 and GITA RM 162,000 match. The placeholders reproduce the Chart 1 case study plus the RM200 fee (80,343 + 149,150 + 200 = 229,693; 48,530 + 122,018 + 200 = 170,748; 58,945 × 12 = 707,340; 229,693 − 250 × 97.06 = 205,428), i.e. an MV General baseline, not the MV ToU default. "3.1 Years" cannot be reproduced from any tariff/GITA combination at default inputs (computed range 1.8 – 7.2 years); it appears hard-coded.
- **Payback formula counts only MD savings from the BESS nameplate.** Payback = net BESS CapEx / (bessKw × mdRate × 12). It ignores solar savings and solar CapEx, assumes the 2-hour battery (kWh = 2 × kW) shaves its full kW rating every month, and ignores the 50% MD floor used in the bill calculation (bessKw 1000 vs MD 900: bill shaves 450 kW, payback divides by 1000 kW). With bessKw = 0 and solar > 0 it shows "0.0 Years"; with no savings it shows "N/A Years". No degradation, O&M, efficiency losses, financing or tariff escalation.
- **GITA in the simulator** is 24% × full BESS CapEx deducted up front. It ignores the "70% statutory income" limit stated in the GITA table and is not applied to solar CapEx, although the same report says integrated solar + BESS gets 100% GITA on the entire system.
- **Fixed fee hard-coded at RM200 for every tariff**, but the tariff table gives RM250/month for HV General and HV ToU.
- **Single blended energy rates**: MV_TOU 0.2886 and HV_TOU 0.4200 RM/kWh with no stated peak/off-peak weighting. Solar offsets kWh at the blended rate and never reduces MD. BESS energy arbitrage is not modelled.
- **CapEx average RM1,350/kWh** is labelled "avg", but the midpoint of the stated RM1,150 – 1,600/kWh benchmark is 1,375.
- **Case-study chart does not reconcile with its own subtitle or the simulator.** The subtitle says 900 kW baseline MD, but Step 1 MD charges 72,795 = 750 kW × 97.06 (900 kW would give 87,354). Step 3's 48,530 = 500 kW × 97.06, i.e. 750 − 250. The 750 kW peak-window MD is never stated. Step 2 energy 113,723 cannot be reproduced from 1 MWp × 115 kWh/kWp at 0.2886 (that gives 111,111). **Energy charges rise from Step 2 (113,723) to Step 3 (122,018) when the BESS is added**, with no explanation. Stack totals (extractor arithmetic, excluding the fee): 229,493 / 217,125 / 186,518 / 170,548.
- **Dispatch visualizer, three different net-grid series.** The initial series is computed with a 100 kW floor (100 at 9:00 and 12:00). The "Standard Peak Shave" button, which is styled active on load, swaps in hard-coded stdNet (70 and 0 at those hours), so clicking the already-active button changes the chart. "Late Afternoon Spike" (heavyNet) differs from stdNet only at 14:00 (510 vs 310), 15:00 (730 vs 580) and 16:00 (720 vs 680). The code comment calls it a "rainstorm solar drop" but the solar series is unchanged. The comment's promised "live toggle controls for Solar and BESS output" do not exist.
- **Dispatch energy does not balance.** bessDischargeStd discharges 1,050 kWh (14:00–18:00) but charges only 400 kWh (10:00–11:00). Charging covers 2 hours, against the card's "Midday Charging (10am–1pm)". No battery size is stated for the visualizer. In every mode the net peak inside 14:00–22:00 is 750 kW (18:00–19:00), against a baseline peak of 980 kW at 15:00. The "dynamic MD target" is never drawn or given a value.
- **Solar mismatch notice is internally inconsistent.** It calls 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM "Off-Peak tariff", but 2:00–3:00 PM is inside the stated 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM peak window.
- **Tariff table internal checks.** Capacity + network = combined MD in every row, and +8.7% reconciles (97.06 / 89.27 = 1.0873). HV energy charges (43.03; 44.52 / 40.43 sen/kWh) are higher than MV (29.83; 31.32 / 27.23) and LV (27.03; 28.52 / 24.43). That is unusual for a voltage-tier structure and worth checking against the primary RP4 schedule. LV capacity and network charges are given in sen/kWh, not RM/kW.
- **GITA table claims have no source.** It says Budget 2027 (2027 – 2030) keeps standalone BESS at Tier 1 100% and standalone solar at Tier 2 60%, and raises integrated solar + BESS to Tier 1 100% for the whole system (also the banner headline). The KB coordinator flagged this as conflicting with other reports in the set; this extract does not check that.
- **Regulatory cards cite nothing.** No citation or link is given for any of them: ST licensing for BESS ≥ 5 kW under Electricity Supply Act 1990; GP/ST/No.62/2026 (IEC 62619, IEC 63056, UL 9540A); Form G / Form H; BOMBA MS 2747:2024 2-hour fire-rated enclosure; CAS for SELCO > 72 kWp; mandatory BESS for new SELCO > 1 MWac; CRESS 14 sen/kWh developers / 4 sen/kWh consumers. All should be verified against primary documents.
- **Provider directory has no sources.** No citation or link supports any provider claim: portfolios, order books, the 20 MWh Perak project, "Global #1", the HyperStrong exclusivity via Plus Xnergy, distributor lists, the 92% efficiency. The modal heading says "Verified ROI Metrics & Impact", yet nothing is verified, and several "roi" fields are not ROI metrics (Sunview: advisory and O&M; Sungrow: product features; HyperStrong: execution time). EVOLTS "Sub-cycle Ride-Through (15-30 min)" is self-contradictory wording.
- **Smaller inconsistencies.** The sizing matrix pairs "15 – 30 Minutes" with "(2C)", but 2C is 30 minutes and 15 minutes would be 4C. The cabinet range "100 kW to 2.5 MW" overlaps the containerized PowerTitan 2.0 (2.5MW/5MWh). The banner's "3–5 Year Payback" contrasts with the simulator's computed 1.8 years at defaults.
- **HTML comment plan vs implementation.** The "Dynamic Stat Ticker" is a static banner. The "dynamic ToU vs General highlight" is static row shading. The "Waterfall" chart is a plain bar chart. "Filter Chips" are only category tabs plus search. There is no separate "Tropical Cooling/Grid-Forming" comparison. The "Step-by-step checklist / Procurement Roadmap" is three cards. No nav tab is highlighted on initial load.

# R4 — Malaysia C&I Solar PV & BESS Market Explorer (2024–2026)

Page header (H1): "Peninsular Malaysia C&I Solar & BESS Market Explorer". Subtitle: "Market Sizing, RP4 Tariff Analysis & Storage Economics (2024–2026)". Status badge: "TNB Supply Area | RP4 Regime Effective Jul 2025 – Dec 2027". Six tabs: Overview & Policy; RP4 Market Sizing; Bill & BESS Simulator; Solar & BESS Deployment; Geographic Explorer; Addressable TAM & Strategy. ## Key claims (index)

- ~1,648,000 C&I accounts in Peninsular Malaysia (LV 98.3%, MV 1.6%, HV 0.04%); 2025 C&I energy sales 110,140 GWh = 76.5% of the Peninsular total of 143,973 GWh (sections 1, 2).
- By RP4 category: LV General ~1,602,300 accts / 26,940 GWh; LV ToU ~18,500 / 1,460; MV General ~19,120 / 34,550; MV ToU ~7,380 / 30,640; HV General ~110 / 3,250; HV ToU ~590 / 13,300 (section 2). MV = 45.3% of total Peninsular demand.
- RP4 (effective 1 July 2025 – Dec 2027) unbundled tariffs into five line items; MV maximum-demand charge RM89.27/kW (General, 24/7) and RM97.06/kW (ToU, 2pm–10pm weekdays), "+115% to +201% under RP4" (sections 1, 3).
- Solar ATAP (live 1 Jan 2026) and revised SELCO: zero export rollover with monthly forfeiture at SMP ~18–20 sen/kWh; BESS mandatory for SELCO systems >1 MWac; SELCO standby charge reduced to RM12/kWp/month; Solar ATAP has no national C&I cap, max 1 MWac/account (section 1).
- NEM 3.0 (NEM NOVA) closed 30 Jun 2025 with 1,417.31 MW subscribed of a 1,700 MW cap (282.69 MW unsubscribed); ~165 MW COD tail in 2026 (sections 1, 4).
- C&I solar additions: ~190 MW (2022), ~305 (2023), ~475 (2024), ~600 (2025), ~710 MW (2026 forecast); cumulative ~2,280 MW 2022–26 (section 4).
- CRESS: >3,000 MW allocated, min 30 MW off-site farm, System Access Charge 20 sen/kWh (firm) vs 40 sen (non-firm), 18–24 month lead time; ~150 MW expected in 2026 (sections 1, 4).
- C&I BESS: ~145–180 MWh cumulative, ~85–110 MWh physically commissioned by mid-2026; Plus Xnergy leads with a 100 MWh portfolio incl. a 20.0 MWh single site (section 4).
- ~12,200 MV industrial customers; Selangor 33–35% and Johor 21–23% (over half of MV industrial load), Penang 14–16%, N. Sembilan & Melaka 8–10%, Perak 7–8%, Kedah 6–7% (section 5).
- TAM 2026–2030: LV 2,500–3,200 MWp solar / 50–100 MWh BESS; MV 6,500–8,500 MWp / 3,500–5,500 MWh; HV >3,000 MW CRESS + 800–1,200 MW onsite / 1,500–2,500 MWh BTM (+3 GWh CRESS) (section 6).
- Target paybacks: LV 3.5–5.0 years, MV 3.0–4.5 years (w/ GITA 100%), HV 3.5–5.5 years (section 6).
- MIDA's GITA 100% tax allowance sunsets 31 December 2026 (section 6).
- Peninsular system peak: 20,066 MW (2024), 21,049 MW (28 May 2025), 21,469 MW (23 Apr 2026) (section 1).
- Simulator default (MV General, 800 kW peak, 250,000 kWh, 250 kW shaved): code computes annual BESS savings RM 272,095 and payback ~2.0 years; the static placeholder shows RM 267,810 and ~3.2 years (Calculators).

## 1. Overview & Policy

### Executive Market Synthesis & RP4 Regime Transition

"Peninsular Malaysia’s Commercial and Industrial (C&I) clean energy landscape underwent a structural regime shift between July 2025 and January 2026. Regulatory Period 4 (RP4), implemented by PETRA and Suruhanjaya Tenaga (ST), unbundled Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) electricity tariffs into five distinct line items and replaced legacy codes (B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3) with voltage-tiered categories (LV, MV, HV General and ToU). Concurrently, the launch of **Solar ATAP** and revised **SELCO guidelines** on 1 January 2026 eliminated multi-month solar export rollovers, enforced monthly credit forfeiture at wholesale System Marginal Price (SMP ~18–20 sen/kWh), and mandated battery storage (BESS) for self-consumption systems exceeding 1 MWac. This dashboard summarizes the macro drivers shaping C&I solar PV and storage sizing in Peninsular Malaysia."

| MV Peak Demand Charge | RM89.27–97.06 | per kW/month (+115% to +201% under RP4) |
| 2026 C&I Solar Additions | ~710 MW | Across Solar ATAP, SELCO & CRESS |

### Malaysia C&I Solar & Wheeling Programme Regulatory Comparison (2026)

Four programme cards (no source links on the cards).

**Solar ATAP** — badge "Live 1 Jan 2026"
- Target: LV & MV Commercial/Industrial
- Quota Cap: No National Cap for C&I
- Sizing Limit: Up to 100% MD (Max 1 MWac/account)
- Export Tariff: SMP Wholesale (~18–20 sen/kWh)
- Rollover: Zero Rollover (Monthly forfeiture)
- Application Workflow: Post-commissioning filing (Forms G & H)

**SELCO (Self-Consumption)** — badge "Updated Jan 2026"
- Target: Large MV & HV Industrial Facilities
- Quota Cap: Uncapped behind-the-meter
- Sizing Limit: Up to 100% MD (No MW upper limit)
- Mandatory BESS: Required for >1 MWac systems
- Standby Charge: Reduced to RM12/kWp/month (>1 MWac)
- Grid Export: Strict 100% zero grid export allowed

**CRESS (Grid Wheeling)** — badge "Expanded Mar 2025"
- Target: HV Malls, Fabs & Hyperscale Data Centres
- Pipeline: >3,000 MW Allocated
- Min Project Size: 30 MW off-site renewable farm
- Access Fee (SAC): 20 sen/kWh (Firm) vs 40 sen (Non-firm)
- Wheeling Model: Direct off-take via TNB grid infrastructure
- Execution Lead: 18–24 months (PSS Stage 1 & 2)

**NEM 3.0 (NEM NOVA)** — badge "Closed 30 Jun 2025"
- Target: Legacy C&I Solar Rooftop
- Final Subscribed: 1,417.31 MW (out of 1,700 MW cap)
- Unsubscribed: 282.69 MW remaining at closure
- Export Settlement: SMP offset against net electricity bill
- Offset Scope: System Marginal Price off-set with 3-mo rollover
- Status: COD tail of ~165 MW completing in 2026

## 3. Bill & BESS Simulator

### Interactive RP4 Monthly Bill & 30-Minute Peak Shaving Simulator

"Under RP4, TNB introduced unbundled charges for Capacity (RM/kW or sen/kWh), Network (RM/kW or sen/kWh), Energy (sen/kWh), Retail (RM20–250/mo), and a volatile monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA). On Medium Voltage (MV General & ToU), Maximum Demand (MD) is billed on the single highest 30-minute average load interval recorded during the billing cycle. Standalone rooftop solar cannot guarantee MD savings because a passing cloud exposes the facility to full demand charges (RM89.27–97.06/kW). Use this tool to simulate monthly bill line items, analyze BESS peak shaving ROI, and factor in GITA 100% tax allowance savings."

Input panel "⚙️ Facility Inputs" (label "RP4 Rates (2025-2027)"): RP4 Tariff Category, Recorded Peak Demand (kW), Monthly Consumption (kWh), BESS Peak Shaving Target (kW), Monthly AFA Rate (sen/kWh). Full input definitions, formulas and computed outputs are under "Calculators and interactive logic".

Panel note: "**Note:** MD charge on MV General is RM89.27/kW (24/7). On MV ToU, MD charge is RM97.06/kW (2pm–10pm weekdays only)."

Result cards (static placeholder text in the HTML, replaced by JS when the tab opens):
- "Base Monthly Electricity Bill" — RM 135,420 — "Without BESS Peak Shaving"
- "Monthly Bill With BESS" — RM 113,102 — "Includes demand shaving & AFA"
- "Annual BESS Utility Savings" — RM 267,810 — "Est. Payback: ~3.2 Years (w/ GITA)"

Chart: "RP4 Bill Component Breakdown: Standard vs BESS Optimized" — caption "Shows how BESS directly slashes the unbundled Capacity & Network Maximum Demand lines."

"Rooftop solar installation in Peninsular Malaysia has transitioned from quota-capped net energy metering (NEM NOVA) to open self-consumption (SELCO) and post-commissioning registration under **Solar ATAP**. ## 5. Geographic Explorer

### Geographic Concentration of Medium Voltage Industrial Customers

"Peninsular Malaysia’s ~12,200 Medium Voltage (11 kV & 33 kV) industrial manufacturing customers are heavily concentrated along the West Coast manufacturing belt and the southern Johor growth corridor. State-level electricity consumption statistics from Suruhanjaya Tenaga confirm that **Selangor (33–35%)** and **Johor (21–23%)** account for over half of total MV industrial load. High rooftop solar penetration in these regions has depressed midday wholesale electricity prices (System Marginal Price), creating a pronounced "duck curve" and making BESS mandatory for local factories looking to capture peak shaving value."
